target_customer: Scientists and IT teams at pharma and biotech companies; originally research labs with lab instruments
problem: Lab instruments produce data locked in proprietary formats and notebooks, so scientists cannot monitor, share or analyze it easily.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS data platform; originally IoT hardware module plus web dashboard
product_category: Scientific data cloud for life sciences

founders.name: Siping Wang
education: MIT, SM in electrical engineering and computer science
founders.background_notes: MIT News (2018-01-25): worked in the Cornell Semiconducting RF Lab and MIT Media Lab; named to Forbes 30 Under 30. YC page lists him as the only founder.

founders.name: Alok Tayi
founders.background_notes: MIT News: former Harvard postdoc in materials science and chemistry, met Wang on a Media Lab project.

founders.name: Salvatore Savo
founders.background_notes: MIT News: former Harvard postdoc who researched IoT in labs with Tayi. Also named as co-founder in Crunchbase coverage of the Series B.

technical_complexity.rationale: The 2015 product paired a custom hardware module, TetraScience Link, with cloud software and security to connect heterogeneous lab instruments. The later data platform must harmonize many proprietary instrument formats.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations to instruments and harmonized data pipelines create switching costs in regulated pharma, though lab informatics vendors could extend their products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Benchling is a later partner: TetraScience supports Benchling integration. No acquisition of TetraScience was found.

market_need_then: YC (2015-08-18) says researchers checked equipment and logged results by hand in notebooks. MIT News (2018) reports adoption by over 70 pharma and biotech firms and over 60 percent of the top 20 pharma.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical enterprise; positioning moved from Tetra R&D Data Cloud to Scientific Data and AI Cloud.

branding.community_and_virality: Featured on Forbes 30 Under 30 and MIT News; the company publishes named pharma customer testimonials.

brand_strength.rationale: Known inside pharma data circles with named customers, but no sourced evidence that the brand itself drove sales.

pivots.from: IoT hardware module and dashboard to monitor lab instruments
pivots.to: Tetra Data Platform, a cloud data platform for pharma R&D data
pivots.why: Crunchbase coverage says today's company differs from the original; another source says its R&D Data Cloud journey began in 2019.

outcome_analysis: TetraScience began as a lab-instrument IoT startup from MIT and Harvard researchers and joined YC Summer 2015. It moved to a cloud data platform for pharma, raised an 8 million dollar Series A in October 2019 and an 80 million dollar Series B in April 2021, and reported 300 percent ARR growth in 2021. It remains private with a possible small round in February 2026 and no exit or layoffs found.
notes: The 2026-02 round appears in CB Insights (14.99M as Series B-II) and Multiples (15M, undisclosed stage) only, so stage is other. A 120K dollar 2015 pre-seed from Y Combinator appears in aggregators only and is not recorded. The seed amount is not found. Another aggregator lists a 15M Series B in 2026 as conflicting. Total raised varies 103M to 117M across aggregators. YC page lists only Siping Wang; Tayi and Savo are named as co-founders by MIT News and Crunchbase. Competitors: the YC launch post names none and no dated 2015 rivals were found. The Tetra Lab Monitoring divestiture of 2021-12 is reported by an aggregator only.
